title: Fair To Middling For Me But Your Mileage May Vary
text:
Fair To Middling For Me But Your Mileage May Vary. These bowls are solidly made and do work well in the microwave. As a 73 year old guy with some health problems though, I do have some issues with them. These issues may or may not apply to you.

The primary issue for me is that the stacked bowls are really stuck together hard. It takes quite a bit of effort for me to peel one bowl off the stack. If the bowls were any less durable, they would rip apart in the process. That's how hard I have to work at it. Prying an edge of a bowl up with a fingernail so I can grab it even hurts a bit.

A couple of other concerns turned out not to be issues at all, though a different hassle did pop up. I used a bowl to heat up a can of Campbell's Chunky Beef Stew. The bowl looked so shallow I wasn't sure it would hold the whole can's worth of stew but it did. If you've ever heated up any of Campbell's Chunky soups in a microwave, you know their soup has a tendency to bubble up and pop, splattering soup around your microwave. I wasn't sure the lid would stay on the bowl the first time I used it. Indeed, I had my fingers crossed that I wouldn't end up with a messy microwave. Well, the snap on lid stay firmly in place and my concern was groundless. That lid did raise another issue though. Taking the hot top off the bowl was another Ouch! to my fingertips.

My last issue with these bowls is one of practical finances. Given my age and health issues, washing dishes is an arduous task for me these days. So I use disposable dishes as much as possible. These bowls are too pricey for me to regularly use them as disposable products though.

Now all these issues are directly related to my age and my physical limitations. As such, they may or may not apply to you and only you can decide if they do or not. So read the other reviews to get a broader picture and make a decision based on your own situation. Good luck.
